Below is a summary of what’s happening, where the violation lives, and a minimal patch to resolve the DAP error:

1) Bug Scenario & Root Cause  
   - DAP reports “The WAI-ARIA widget with IMG role must have a nonempty alternate text or a label.”  
   - In our `<Search>` component, the magnifier icon is rendered as an `<svg>` (via `<Search16 … role="img" />`) with no `aria-label`, no `aria-labelledby`, and not hidden.  
   - Either we must give it an accessible name or, since it is purely decorative (the visible label “Search” is read by screen readers), we should hide it from assistive technology.

2) Location of the fix  
   - `packages/react/src/components/Search/Search.js`  
   - In the `render()` method, right at the `<Search16 className=… role="img" />` line.

3) Patch  
   - Remove the `role="img"` (so it no longer gets treated as an interactive graphic)  
   - Add `aria-hidden="true"` (so screen readers ignore it)  
   - Add `focusable="false"` (to prevent IE11/SVG focus issues)

```javascript
### packages/react/src/components/Search/Search.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
        <Search16 className={`${prefix}--search-magnifier`} role="img" />
        <label htmlFor={id} className={`${prefix}--label`}>
          {labelText}
        </label>
=======
        <Search16
          className={`${prefix}--search-magnifier`}
          aria-hidden="true"
          focusable="false"
        />
        <label htmlFor={id} className={`${prefix}--label`}>
          {labelText}
        </label>
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With this change, the SVG is correctly treated as a decorative icon, and the DAP violation will no longer occur.
